title: Jev names a primary and a backup, and a run that cannot start on the first runs on the second
name: backup
description: `modelQuestion`/`jevChoice` in packages/core/src/jev.ts ask Jev for one name. Ask for two: `model` and `backup`, the backup on a different host than the primary whenever the candidate list has one (say so in the question text, and reject a backup equal to the primary). When the primary is on the `openrouter` host, the backup is a `claude` or `codex` model, never another `openrouter` one: free models share an upstream pool and rate-limit together. Carry both into the run record — packages/schema/src/run.ts gains `backup: string | null` and `ran: 'primary' | 'backup'` (schema version bump per the schema's own rules, migration for old records defaulting to `ran: 'primary'`). In `dispatch()`: `checkHost` and the availability probe (host-avail) on the primary; a refusal switches to the backup's line before the worktree; and if the primary's process exits before its first tool line with a limit/auth classification (`limitSpent` from host-avail — for `openrouter`, a 429 left after the loop's bounded retry), the same worktree is re-run on the backup once and the record says `ran: 'backup'` with the primary's reason in a `fellBack` field. No backup available → today's refusal, unchanged. `sober status`, `sober logs` header and the dashboard run line (node sober-status-sober-logs-and-the-run-pane-0o4s renders them) read the new fields; keep that node's surface change out of here, only make the data available. Tests: jev.test.ts for the two-name question, the same-host rejection and the openrouter → claude/codex rule; dispatch.test.ts for switch-before-start and fall-after-start with a fake host that prints the captured limit text; schema migration test.

brief.approach:
**1. Jev picks two names — `packages/core/src/jev.ts`.** `JevDecision` gains `backup: string | null`. `askJev` asks for the primary as it does today (`modelQuestion` → `jevChoice` among `modelsFor(ask.models, complexity)`). Then a pure `backupCandidates(models, primary, complexity)` builds the backup set out of `ask.models` (the whole available list, not only the entries that cover the score). It drops the primary. It keeps only entries on a different host (`adapterFor(m.run).id`) when there are any. When the primary is on `openrouter`, it keeps only `claude`/`codex` entries, because free models share one upstream pool. Entries that cover the score go first. If none of them cover it, the other hosts' entries are used. A new `backupQuestion(candidates)` asks for one `backup` choice. Its text says it is the fallback when the primary cannot start, on a different host. The existing `jevChoice` checks the answer against that set, so a backup equal to the primary or a second `openrouter` is off the list and is a `JevError`. The existing rule holds: shown only allowed options, Jev cannot pick a wrong one. Zero candidates means `backup: null` and no call. One candidate means that one, no call. So this is three round trips at most.

**2. The score-only path gets the same backup.** In `packages/core/src/dispatch.ts`, when `jevMode` is off, `chooseLine` stays as it is and the backup is `backupCandidates(available, primary, complexity)[0]`. Both paths use one rule.

**3. Switch before start — `dispatch()`.** `checkHost(line)` for the primary as today. If it refuses (`!host.ok`), or the availability probe already marked the primary's host spent, and a backup exists, `checkHost(backup)` runs. If that one is ready, the backup becomes the line before `addWorktree`/`startRun`. The record gets `ran: 'backup'` and `fellBack: <the primary's reason>`. No backup, or a backup that is also not ready: the same `refused(...)` error as today, word for word. `UnknownHostError` does not fall back (a typo is a config error, not an outage).

**4. Fall after start — also `dispatch()`.** `onLine` already sees every raw line. A flag `sawTool` is set when `renderLine(JSON.parse(line))` yields a `kind: 'tool'` line (the parse is in a try/catch, and a line that is not JSON is ignored). The raw output is also kept in a bounded buffer. When `startAgent` returns `failed`, and `!sawTool`, and `limitSpent(adapterFor(line).id, buffer + exit.reason)` is non-null, and a backup exists and `checkHost(backup)` is ok: `startAgent` runs **once** more with `host: backup` in the **same** worktree and the same run id and log, after one `raw` separator line (`primary <line> stopped: <reason> — running on <backup>`). The second exit is final: no third try. A stop or a timeout never falls back.

**5. OpenRouter's 429 uses the same one pattern.** `packages/cli/src/agent.ts` (`sober agent`): when the loop's failure is a 429 left after `MAX_RETRIES` (`packages/core/src/agent.ts` returns `answered 429: …`), it writes `spent: <reason>` on stderr, next to the plain reason. Then `openrouterSpent` in `packages/core/src/hosts.ts` reads the probe and a run with one regex, and the limit text still lives in one place per adapter.

**6. The run record — `packages/schema/src/run.ts`.** Three defaulted fields, like `attended`/`tier`: `backup: z.string().nullable().default(null)`, `ran: z.enum(['primary','backup']).default('primary')`, `fellBack: z.string().nullable().default(null)`. The run record is local and read, not migrated (§5.5, and the file's own comment). `SCHEMA_VERSION` versions board records only, so it is **not** bumped, and "migration" here means an old record parses with `ran: 'primary'`. The node text asks for a version bump, but the schema's own rules say otherwise, so I follow the rules. `packages/core/src/run.ts`: `startRun` takes `backup`/`ran`/`fellBack`. `finishRun`'s `RunResult` may set `host`, `ran` and `fellBack`, so a fall after start rewrites `host` to the line that really ran. The run record's `host` stays what it is documented as: "the exact line that ran".

**7. Out of scope.** `sober status`, the `sober logs` header and the dashboard run line render nothing new here. That is node sober-status-sober-logs-and-the-run-pane-0o4s. This node only makes the fields exist and fills them in.

**Tests.**
- `packages/core/src/jev.test.ts`: the backup question shows only entries on another host. It never shows the primary. An `openrouter` primary gets only claude/codex candidates. A backup choice off that set is a `JevError`. 0 and 1 candidates cost no extra call.
- `packages/core/src/dispatch.test.ts`, with the fake hosts the file already uses:
  - (a) a primary whose `checkHost` refuses runs on the backup, and the record has `ran: 'backup'` and `fellBack`.
  - (b) a primary that prints the captured Codex "You've hit your usage limit." text and exits before any tool line is re-run on the backup in the same worktree. The record's `host` is the backup's line.
  - (c) the same exit after a tool line is **not** re-run.
  - (d) no backup gives today's refusal message, unchanged.
- `packages/schema/src/run.test.ts`: a record with none of the three fields parses to `backup: null, ran: 'primary', fellBack: null`. An unknown `ran` value is refused.

acceptance.run: pnpm --filter @besober/schema build && pnpm vitest run packages/schema/src/run.test.ts
acceptance.proves: an old run record still parses, as ran: 'primary' with no backup, and the three new fields are checked

acceptance.run: pnpm --filter @besober/core build && pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/jev.test.ts
acceptance.proves: Jev is asked for a backup only among entries on another host, never the primary, and never another openrouter entry when the primary is openrouter; an answer off that list fails

acceptance.run: pnpm --filter @besober/core build && pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/dispatch.test.ts
acceptance.proves: a refused primary switches to the backup before the worktree; a limit-classified exit before the first tool line re-runs once on the backup in the same worktree; an exit after a tool line does not; with no backup the refusal is today's

acceptance.run: pnpm --filter @besober/core build && pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/hosts.test.ts packages/cli/src/agent.test.ts
acceptance.proves: a 429 left after the loop's retries is written as `spent:` and read by the same openrouterSpent pattern the probe uses
the new fields and signatures typecheck everywhere they are read, and the change passes biome
